verdicts.claim: SQLite performs automatic passive checkpoints by default when the WAL reaches 1000 pages (Overview)
verdicts.evidence: Overview is uncited; wal.html §2.1: 'By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages' and §3.2 auto checkpoints are PASSIVE.

verdicts.claim: The default automatic checkpoint threshold is 1000 pages; automatic checkpoints are triggered during a COMMIT that exceeds this size or when the last database connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes.' (c1-4 returned 403)

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpointing is the default mode for automatic checkpoints
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §3.2: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.'

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE copies as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers, and the busy-handler is never invoked
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: 'Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers... The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode.'

verdicts.claim: FULL checkpointing blocks (via the busy-handler) until no writer exists and all readers are using the most recent snapshot, then checkpoints all frames and syncs
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: 'blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the database file.'

verdicts.claim: RESTART behaves like FULL but additionally blocks until all readers are reading from the database file only, so the next writer restarts the log
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: 'blocks ... until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE checkpointing follows the RESTART procedure and then truncates the WAL file to zero bytes before returning successfully
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: 'works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP (-1) performs no checkpointing work and is used exclusively to query the current size of the WAL and checkpointed frames
verdicts.evidence: c_checkpoint_full: '#define SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP -1 /* Do no work at all */'; wal_checkpoint_v2: 'The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned ... via *pnLog and *pnCkpt.'

verdicts.claim: Long-lived read transactions can cause 'checkpoint starvation', where the WAL grows without bound because the checkpointer cannot advance
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6 Checkpoint starvation: 'if ... there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'; §2.2 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress.' (c1-5 only partially supports)

verdicts.claim: A critical concurrency bug in the checkpointer that could lead to data loss or corruption was fixed in March 2026
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §11: 'On 2026-03-03 ... found and fixed a bug that could, in rare cases, lead to database corruption ... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)'; triggers when two connections 'write or checkpoint at the same instant'. Note: SQLite calls it 'not an emergency', so 'critical' overstates; c1-4 returned 403.

notes: All five cited URLs were cache misses; 5 WebFetches used, 0 WebSearches.
c1-4 (theconsensus.dev) returned HTTP 403; claims citing it were decided via co-cited sqlite.org/wal.html.
c1-5 (sqliteforum.com) only partially supports the starvation claim: no 'checkpoint starvation' term, no 'without bound'; primary support is wal.html.

Troubleshooting claim wording 'critical' and 'data loss' overstates the source; SQLite says 'rare', 'database corruption', and 'this is not an emergency'. Version 3.51.3 and backports 3.44.6/3.50.7 omitted from draft.
